topic: Light: Convex Lens Aperture & Image Formation (Pre-to-Post Intervention)

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Convex lens forms real candle image on screen; lower half covered with black cardboard.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Bottom half of the flame disappears from the screen.

ordered_attempts.question_stem: PhET Simulation: Student manipulates rays and covers half of lens.
ordered_attempts.student_response: I see that rays from the top and bottom of the arrow still hit the open top half and meet at the screen. The image is whole, just darker!

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Reassessment: Circular coin taped over center 20% of concave mirror.
ordered_attempts.student_response: The entire tree image will still be seen on the wall, but its brightness will be slightly reduced because light from all parts of the tree reflects off the rest of the mirror.

evidence_summary: Q1: Demonstrated classic half-lens blocking fallacy
Step 2: Interactive POE simulation induced conceptual shift
Step 3: Flawless isomorphic near-transfer to concave mirror
